This application, under Section 482 of Cr.P.C, has been filed for quashment of FIR in Crime No.

294, 506 and 34 of IPC.
2. Undisputed facts are that applicants are in-laws of son of complainant Vidya Singh Bhadoriya /

sentences.text: Then, they started abusing her filthily in the name of mother and sister.
When she objected to it, then she was beaten by the all three of them by fist and blows.
As a result, she sustained injury on her left hand.

When she raised an alarm, her neighbours Pradeep Singh Bhadoriya and Punit Tomar came and intervened in the matter, and all the three persons, while fleeing away, extended a threat that the amount be paid otherwise she would be killed.

Since her husband was out of Gwalior city, thereforfe, she could not lodge the report immediately and accordingly the FIR was lodged on 15.01.2024.
4.
Challenging the FIR lodged by respondent No. 2, it is submitted by counsel for applicants that in fact, aforesaid FIR is by way of counterblast.
Daughter of applicant No. 1 is the daughter-in-law of complainant.
She was treated with cruelty by the complainant and other family members.

Therefore,
daughter of applicant No. 1 had lodged an FIR on 13.09.2022 at Police Station Navghar, District Mira Bhaidar, Basai Virar for offences under Sections 498A, 377, 406, 323, 504, 506, and 34 of IPC.
Daughter of applicant No. 1 has also filed a petition for divorce on 14.10.2021.
Similarly, on 18.07.2022, an application under Section 125 of the CrPC has also been filed by the daughter of applicant No. 1.

A complaint under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act has been instituted by daughter of applicant No. 1 against respondent No. 2 as well as other in-laws, namely Vikas Singh Bhadauria, Rajesh Singh Bhadauria, Ravi Singh Bhadauria, and Mrs.

The Supreme Court in the case of Rishipal Singh v. State of U.P. reported in (2014) 7 SCC 215 has held as under:-
11.

entities.text: Rishipal Singh v. State of U.P. reported in (2014) 7 SCC 215
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court in Medchl Chemicals & Pharma (P) Ltd. v. Biological E. Ltd. [(2000) 3 SCC 269 : 2000 SCC (Cri) 615] has discussed at length about the scope and ambit while exercising power under Section 482 CrPC and how cautious and careful the approach of the courts should be.

entities.text: Medchl Chemicals & Pharma (P) Ltd. v. Biological E. Ltd. [(2000) 3 SCC 269 : 2000 SCC (Cri) 615]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We deem it apt to extract the relevant portion from that judgment, which reads: (SCC p. 272, para 2) "2. Exercise of jurisdiction under the inherent power as envisaged in Section 482 of the Code to have the complaint or the charge-sheet quashed is an exception rather than a rule and the case for quashing at the initial stage must have to be treated as the rarest of rare so as not to scuttle the prosecution.
With the lodgement of first information report the ball is set to roll and thenceforth the law takes its own course and the investigation ensues in accordance with the provisions of law.
The jurisdiction as such is rather limited and restricted and its undue expansion is neither practicable nor warranted.

In the event, however, the court on a perusal of the complaint comes to a conclusion that the allegations levelled in the complaint or charge-sheet on the face of it does not constitute or disclose any offence as alleged,
there ought not to be any hesitation to rise up to the expectation of the people and deal with the situation as is required under the law.

Frustrated litigants ought not to be indulged to give vent to their vindictiveness through a legal process and such an investigation ought not to be allowed to be continued since the same is opposed to the concept of justice, which is paramount".
(Emphasis supplied)
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:7931
Thus, it is clear that quashing of complaint or charge sheet or FIR is an exception and it is to be done in the rarest of rare cases.
It is true that if the complaint makes out a cognizable offence, then mala fides of complainant becomes secondary.
Whether FIR has been launched by a frustrated litigant or not can always be considered by this Court.

8. In light of the judgment passed by Supreme Court in the case of Rishipal Singh (supra), if the facts of the present case are considered, then it is clear that on the FIR lodged by daughter of applicant No. 1, respondent No. 2 and other in-laws are facing trial for offences under Sections 498A, 377, 406, 323, 504, 506 and 34 of IPC.
Similarly, daughter of applicant No. 1 has also filed a divorce petition against son of respondent No. 2.
An application under Section 125 of CrPC has also been filed by the daughter of applicant No. 1 against her husband, i.e., son of respondent No. 2.
A complaint under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act is also pending against respondent No. 2 as well as other in-laws of the daughter of applicant No. 1.

sentences.text: All these proceedings were initiated much prior to lodging of FIR in question.
Furthermore, in light of allegations made in the present FIR, it is clear that not only the FIR is delayed but the allegations are superficial.
Thus, it can be said that the same is by way of counterblast to the different proceedings which have been initiated by daughter of applicant No. 1.

It is true that since respondent No. 2 had specifically mentioned in the FIR that applicant No. 1 is father of her Nirmal Singh Mertia vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176478592/
3 daughter-in-law, therefore police should have conducted a preliminary enquiry but in absence of preliminary enquiry, it cannot be said that FIR is bad.

entities.text: Nirmal Singh Mertia vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since this Court has come to a conclusion that the FIR in question has been lodged by way of counterblast to the proceedings initiated by daughter of applicant No. 1, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:7931 and looking to the trivial nature of allegations made in the FIR, this Court is of considered opinion that the continuation of FIR as well as investigation would be nothing but misuse of lawful authority of the investigating Agency or the Court.

9. Accordingly, FIR in Crime No. 13/2024 registered at Police Station University, District Gwalior,
for offences under Sections 323, 294, 506, and 34 of IPC is hereby quashed.
10. Application succeeds and is, hereby, allowed.

(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE (and)
